payload.claim: witness_gate reads only `tests_result.status` and never `tests_result.collected` to confirm that `criterion.witness` was actually the node the `tests` gate ran under the mutant. `contract.py` (lines 69-75) explicitly distinguishes `collected=None` (did not enumerate) from `collected=[]` (enumerated nothing) as different facts precisely because a bare pass/fail can mean 'ran and behaved this way' or 'nothing matching this name ran at all' — and `criteria.py`'s `_side`/`_green` and `revert.py`'s explicit `collected & failed` checks both guard against exactly this before trusting a status. If a mutant causes the named witness to drop out of collection (e.g. it alters a parametrize count, a skip condition, or an import path) and the repo's `tests` gate reports that as `status="pass"` with zero collected/zero failed (a legitimate reading of the contract, not this repo's own `.saffron/gates/tests.py` quirk), witness_gate records it as `survived` — 'ran and passed with its mutant applied' — when the witness never ran at all. Absence and a genuine pass are treated alike, and the mutant-testing gate this diff adds is the one place that distinction is supposed to matter.
